# SNACK LINE — INTERNATIONAL MARKET ENTRY
## Concept Portfolio, Market-Selection Rationale & Development Plan
**Prepared for Product Council | Version 1.0**

---

> ⚠️ **Status and compliance caveat.** Everything below is a **planning input, not a legal or regulatory opinion**. Snack food is governed by market-specific labelling, additive, allergen, front-of-pack and children's-marketing law that is under active reform in all three markets discussed (Japan's additive-free labelling guidance, Mexico's NOM-051 warning-seal and school-sales regime, Indonesia's staged mandatory halal certification). No recipe, pack, name or claim may be locked until (a) local regulatory counsel has signed the specific SKU in writing, (b) the formulation has been through a local sensory panel, and (c) the first-listing retailer has confirmed the pack format and price architecture. Figures marked *[ILL]* are illustrative planning numbers to be replaced in Gate 1.
>
> **Planning FX (fixed for this document, re-fixed at each gate):** ¥155 = US$1.00 · MXN 17.5 = US$1.00 · IDR 16,200 = US$1.00

---

## 1. Recommendation in One Page

**Recommended primary market: Japan.** Highest margin per unit, most sophisticated snack-innovation infrastructure, and a retail calendar (the convenience-store limited-edition cycle) that rewards a fast, flavour-led newcomer. Also the hardest — which is why we enter with a *narrow, occasion-owned* line rather than a broad flavour range.

**Recommended secondary markets: Mexico (Wave 2) and Indonesia (Wave 3).** Both have a structural opening created by regulation and price architecture respectively, and both can be served from a different manufacturing base than Japan.

**The strategic principle for all three:** we do **not** launch "our snacks, localised." We launch **snacks designed around a local eating occasion that incumbents have under-served**, using our manufacturing capability (baking/extrusion/roasting) as the enabler rather than the idea.

**The line architecture principle — the 80/20 familiarity rule.** Every SKU is *familiar in one axis and novel in one axis, never both*. A familiar local flavour in a novel format, or a novel flavour in an utterly familiar format. Snacks that are strange twice die at second purchase.

| Criterion | Weight | Why it matters for snacks specifically |

| Occasion whitespace | 20% | We need an under-served *moment*, not an under-served flavour |
| Retail access for a newcomer | 20% | Shelf is the binding constraint; listing mechanics differ wildly |
